routes.description: THE Encontro das Águas circuit — from the historic floating port east along the Manaus waterfront to the confluence where the black Rio Negro and sandy Solimões run side by side unmixed (OSM confluence point -3.1189,-59.8927), landing at Porto da CEASA. Straight-line pier-to-pier is 5.4 nm; 8.4 nm reflects the tour track out along the confluence line and back into the CEASA channel. Tour boats and CEASA fast launches work this water daily.

The captive south-bank crossing: Manaus's only link to Careiro da Várzea and the BR-319 corridor, running all day 04:30–20:00 (vehicle balsas + lanchas, ANTAQ-approved fares). Haversine 5.3 nm plus ~10% channel margin for crossing the confluence mixing line.

City-centre feeder to the south bank along the lane worked by regional lanchas and ajatos from the Manaus Moderna quays; passes the full length of the Encontro das Águas. Haversine 9.8 nm plus channel-following margin.

The Rio Negro gateway run — ACAMDAF cooperative lanchas already carry beach-goers, river-community residents and lodge guests from Marina do Davi up the black-water river to Praia do Tupé inside the REDES do Tupé reserve. Haversine 8.7 nm plus ~10% margin for following the north-bank channel. The template for all west-bank community and jungle-lodge transfers.

Cross-town waterfront line from the floating port to the Ponta Negra beach and hotel zone — the water route runs straight where the road grid congests. Haversine 6.3 nm plus margin for the riverfront sweep past São Raimundo. Requires a light landing float at Ponta Negra (none verified today).

Centre-to-Ponta-Negra line terminating at the established Marina do Davi cooperative hub — connects the cruise/regional port directly to the Rio Negro excursion gateway. Haversine 7.0 nm plus ~10% river-bend margin.
Beach-to-beach leisure spur linking the city's flagship urban beach to the Tupé river beaches — extends the Rio Negro leisure mesh. Haversine 9.0 nm plus north-bank channel margin.
Short hospitality spur between the cooperative marina and the historic Tropical Hotel landing — live only if the resort complex redevelopment restores guest operations (status candidate).

Revival of the historic São Raimundo↔Cacau Pirêra (Iranduba) crossing, dormant since the Rio Negro bridge opened in 2011 — a candidate mid-town cross-river spur if Iranduba-side demand returns. Haversine 3.3 nm plus small channel margin.

Tarumã leisure spur from the Ponta Negra hotel zone up into the Tarumã-Açu inlet's private-marina cluster — rounds out the Rio Negro recreational mesh and a charging-host candidate. Haversine 2.0 nm plus inlet-entry margin.
